limitations: Identical independent habitats and forced assignment of all stock
One-generation expected Ricker recruitment rather than long-run persistence
Continuous stock, fixed crowding and recruitment coefficients
Historical priority may be affected by uninspected supplementary analysis or general nonconcave allocation literature
scientific_integrity: All-m integer theorem proved by reduction of the compact simplex to two stationary families and a one-crossing comparison, with finite numerical tests supplementary. Originality is conditional on accessible prior literature. No independent validation or field calibration.
title: A first-order Ricker recruitment allocation transition on three or more identical spawning habitats
